observations.meaning: Magnitude and profile of spectral eigengaps across candidate resolutions within each set, with the screening resolution indicating where the dominant gap lies.

The dominant gap therefore sits at the single-cluster resolution, so this screening calculation is dominated by the single-cluster resolution and does not show a dominant multi-cluster subdivision signal within either set.

cross_modal_consistency.dimension_interpretation: Across the four-view fused patient geometry, the current two-set partition is represented by two substantial, similarly sized groups (55 and 48 patients) with almost identical internal cohesion (mean within-affinity about 0.0093 in each). The boundary between them is only weakly expressed: mean between-affinity (about 0.0090) is barely lower than the within-set values, so the two sets are not sharply separated in this geometry. The internal spectral screening for each set is dominated by the single-cluster resolution (screen_candidate_k = 1 in both), with a large leading eigengap and negligible subsequent gaps; this describes the dominance of a single-cluster resolution within each set and does not constitute evidence of internal multi-cluster substructure. Because no feasible k>=2 set-level solutions or their measurements were supplied, no interpretation of internal subdivision is possible from these results. Taken together, the measurements indicate that the two memberships are internally coherent and comparable in cohesion, while their mutual boundary is weak; this is a statement about geometry concordance, not about biological agreement, and it neither recommends merging the sets nor splitting them.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0001, the set-versus-rest RNA enrichment analysis is estimable and yields a coherent down-regulated signaling phenotype relative to the rest of the partition. The strongest and most statistically adjusted signal is reduced Wnt/beta-catenin signaling (NES -1.79, q about 0.0016), followed by reduced pancreas beta-cell (NES -1.57, q about 0.024), mitotic spindle (NES -1.47, q about 0.034), UV-response-down (NES -1.48, q about 0.037), and TGF-beta signaling (NES -1.49, q about 0.041). These five pathways are all down-regulated with moderate-to-large negative NES values and adjusted q-values below 0.05, and their leading-edge gene lists overlap (for example CTNNB1, NCOR2, JAG1, and NOTCH-family genes appear in both Wnt and TGF-beta sets), which suggests a partially shared signaling theme rather than unrelated isolated hits. The leading up-regulated program is interferon alpha response (NES 1.43), but its adjusted q-value is about 0.35, so its adjusted evidence is considerably weaker than the down-regulated signals. The contrast uses 55 patients in K2_C0001 versus 48 in the rest, so the sample support is balanced and substantial. Overall, the measurements indicate that K2_C0001 has an interpretable biological phenotype characterized mainly by lower expression of Wnt/beta-catenin, TGF-beta, mitotic spindle, UV-response-down, and pancreas beta-cell programs relative to the rest of the partition, with a weaker and less adjusted up-regulation of interferon alpha response. These are relative set-versus-rest rankings and adjusted statistical evidence, not proof of biological importance or clinical meaning.

VHL mutation is strongly depleted in K2_C0001 (18/55 mutated versus 38/48 in rest; odds ratio about 0.13, adjusted q about 4.5e-05), and PBRM1 mutation is also depleted (14/55 versus 25/48; odds ratio about 0.31, adjusted q about 0.028). Among non-driver-panel genes, ATM mutation is absent in K2_C0001 and present in the rest (0/55 versus 6/48; adjusted q about 0.028). The driver-panel results cover only 6 of 15 configured genes because 9 configured genes were not in the selected features, so the panel is a partial post-hoc annotation rather than a comprehensive driver survey. Overall, the measurements indicate that K2_C0001 is characterized by lower VHL and PBRM1 mutation prevalence and higher BAP1 mutation prevalence relative to the rest of the partition, with additional weaker differences in MTOR, KDM5C, SETD2, and ATM. These are relative prevalence differences and adjusted statistical evidence, not proof of biological importance or clinical meaning.

Continuous factors with significant adjusted associations are CT slice thickness (epsilon squared about 0.066, q about 0.026) and CT z-spacing (epsilon squared about 0.048, q about 0.028). These results indicate that membership is associated with several site and acquisition factors, particularly tissue source site and CT phase/scanner model, and with some CT geometry parameters. Association is not causation, and these measurements do not establish that any factor causes or explains the partition; conversely, the nonsignificant factors do not prove absence of confounding. reports.dimension_interpretation: For the current two-set partition, the known-label echo analysis shows small-to-moderate associations with clinical stratification variables and low-to-moderate correspondence with established ccRCC taxonomies. Clinical grade is associated with membership (Cramer's V about 0.22, p about 0.032), with G4 more frequent in K2_C0001 (14 versus 3). Clinical stage is associated (V about 0.27, p about 0.018), with stage III and IV more frequent in K2_C0001 (16 and 12 versus 7 and 3). Clinical T stage is associated (V about 0.25, p about 0.021), with T3 more frequent in K2_C0001 (22 versus 8). Clinical M stage is associated (V about 0.20, p about 0.026), with M1 more frequent in K2_C0001 (11 versus 3), and 5 patients have missing M stage. For molecular taxonomies, the candidate partition shows low-to-moderate correspondence with TCGA m1-m4 (ARI about 0.15, AMI about 0.13, reference n 84), with m1 concentrated in K2_C0002 (25 versus 5) and m3/m4 more frequent in K2_C0001. It also shows low-to-moderate correspondence with ClearCode34 (ARI about 0.24, AMI about 0.18, reference n 76), with ccA concentrated in K2_C0002 (29 versus 9) and ccB more frequent in K2_C0001 (28 versus 10). These results indicate that the partition has some correspondence with clinical severity variables and with established expression-derived taxonomies, but the agreement is not strong. TCGA m1-m4 and ClearCode34 overlap the RNA discovery view, so these are taxonomy correspondence analyses, not independent validation. reports.dimension_interpretation: For K2_C0002, the WXS mutation enrichment analysis is estimable and shows a coherent pattern of mutation prevalence differences relative to the rest of the partition, concentrated in known ccRCC driver genes. VHL mutation is strongly enriched in K2_C0002 (38/48 mutated versus 18/55 in rest; odds ratio about 7.8, adjusted q about 4.5e-05), and PBRM1 mutation is also enriched (25/48 versus 14/55; odds ratio about 3.2, adjusted q about 0.028). In contrast, BAP1 mutation is absent in K2_C0002 (0/48 versus 13/55 in rest; odds ratio 0, adjusted q about 0.001). MTOR, KDM5C, and SETD2 show small differences with wide confidence intervals and adjusted q-values above 0.05, so their adjusted evidence is weak. Among non-driver-panel genes, ATM mutation is present in K2_C0002 and absent in the rest (6/48 versus 0/55; adjusted q about 0.028). The driver-panel results cover only 6 of 15 configured genes because 9 configured genes were not in the selected features, so the panel is a partial post-hoc annotation rather than a comprehensive driver survey. Overall, the measurements indicate that K2_C0002 is characterized by higher VHL and PBRM1 mutation prevalence and absent BAP1 mutation relative to the rest of the partition, with additional weaker differences in MTOR, KDM5C, SETD2, and ATM. These are relative prevalence differences and adjusted statistical evidence, not proof of biological importance or clinical meaning.
reports.cross_evidence_context: A prior Evidence Report for this round covers structural diagnostics for the same two-set partition. That report described two substantial, similarly sized sets with comparable internal cohesion but only a weak mutual boundary in the fused patient-affinity geometry, and it explicitly did not assess biological agreement. The current WXS mutation results are complementary in that they describe mutation prevalence differences for K2_C0002 relative to the rest, whereas the prior report described geometric cohesion and separation. There is no direct conflict, but the two reports address different dimensions: the prior geometry does not establish biological distinctness, and the current mutation enrichment does not establish geometric separation. No prior report addresses WXS mutation enrichment for K2_C0002, so this is the first mutation-based biological-support evidence for this set in the supplied context.
limitations: The WXS driver panel is a post-hoc annotation, not a feature-selection criterion, and only 6 of 15 configured driver genes were available in the selected features.
Mutation enrichment is a set-versus-rest prevalence comparison; it does not establish causality, clinical utility, or independent replication.
Adjusted q-values are multiple-testing-adjusted statistical evidence and do not by themselves establish biological importance.
Several genes (MTOR, KDM5C, SETD2) have wide confidence intervals and adjusted q-values above 0.05, so their adjusted evidence is weak.
The ATM odds ratio is infinite because there are zero mutations in the rest group, and its confidence interval is wide, so the magnitude should be interpreted cautiously.
The contrast uses 48 versus 55 samples; results may be sensitive to sample composition and mutation calling.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For the current two-set partition, several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors show statistically significant associations with candidate membership after multiple-testing correction, while others do not. The largest categorical association is with tissue source site (Cramer's V about 0.43, q about 0.009), followed by CT phase (V about 0.32, q about 0.028) and CT scanner model (V about 0.31, q about 0.028). Continuous factors with significant adjusted associations are CT slice thickness (epsilon squared about 0.066, q about 0.026) and CT z-spacing (epsilon squared about 0.048, q about 0.028). Factors without significant adjusted association include CT manufacturer (V about 0.11, q about 0.22), CT reconstruction kernel (V about 0.20, q about 0.11), CT pixel spacing (epsilon squared about 0.025, q about 0.092), and study year (epsilon squared about 0.007, q about 0.22). These results indicate that membership is associated with several site and acquisition factors, particularly tissue source site and CT phase/scanner model, and with some CT geometry parameters. Association is not causation, and these measurements do not establish that any factor causes or explains the partition; conversely, the nonsignificant factors do not prove absence of confounding. The sample size is 103 for all factors, so coverage is complete for the measured variables, but the contingency tables show imbalanced level distributions (for example, tissue source site and CT phase have uneven counts across sets), which contributes to the associations.
reports.cross_evidence_context: A prior Evidence Report for this round covers structural diagnostics for the same two-set partition, describing two substantial, similarly sized sets with comparable internal cohesion but only a weak mutual boundary in the fused patient-affinity geometry. That report did not address technical or acquisition confounding. The current confounder association results are complementary in that they identify measured site and acquisition factors that are statistically associated with membership, which is relevant context for interpreting the weak geometric boundary. There is no direct conflict, but the two reports address different dimensions: the prior geometry does not establish confounding, and the current associations do not establish that the geometry is driven by these factors. No prior report addresses confounder association for this partition, so this is the first confounder-association evidence in the supplied context.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For the current two-set partition, the representation-effect analysis shows that several measured technical, acquisition, and site factors are associated with variation in the CT or fused representation geometry, with varying effect magnitudes. The largest effect is CT scanner model, associated with about 16.5% of CT representation-geometry variation (permutation p about 0.001, q about 0.0013). CT reconstruction kernel is associated with about 9.5% (p about 0.05, q about 0.05), CT phase with about 8.6% (p about 0.001, q about 0.0013), and tissue source site with about 5.0% of fused representation-geometry variation (p about 0.001, q about 0.0013). Smaller but still significant associations include CT manufacturer (about 2.8%), CT z-spacing (about 2.1%), CT slice thickness (about 2.0%), study year (about 1.5%), and CT pixel spacing (about 1.1%). These results indicate that the representation geometry contains measurable variation associated with scanner model, reconstruction kernel, phase, and site, with scanner model showing the largest single-factor effect. Association is not causation, and these measurements do not establish that any factor causes or explains the partition; they also do not establish that the partition is free of confounding. The sample size is 103 for all factors, so coverage is complete for the measured variables, but the factor levels are imbalanced (for example, 16 scanner models and 10 reconstruction kernels), which can affect effect estimates.

No prior report addresses confounder representation effects for this partition, so this is the first such evidence in the supplied context.

reports.dimension_interpretation: For the current two-set partition, the known-label echo analysis shows small-to-moderate associations with clinical stratification variables and low-to-moderate correspondence with established ccRCC taxonomies. Clinical grade is associated with membership (Cramer's V about 0.22, p about 0.032), with G4 more frequent in K2_C0001 (14 versus 3). Clinical stage is associated (V about 0.27, p about 0.018), with stage III and IV more frequent in K2_C0001 (16 and 12 versus 7 and 3). Clinical T stage is associated (V about 0.25, p about 0.021), with T3 more frequent in K2_C0001 (22 versus 8). Clinical M stage is associated (V about 0.20, p about 0.026), with M1 more frequent in K2_C0001 (11 versus 3), and 5 patients have missing M stage. For molecular taxonomies, the candidate partition shows low-to-moderate correspondence with TCGA m1-m4 (ARI about 0.15, AMI about 0.13, reference n 84), with m1 concentrated in K2_C0002 (25 versus 5) and m3/m4 more frequent in K2_C0001. It also shows low-to-moderate correspondence with ClearCode34 (ARI about 0.24, AMI about 0.18, reference n 76), with ccA concentrated in K2_C0002 (29 versus 9) and ccB more frequent in K2_C0001 (28 versus 10). These results indicate that the partition has some correspondence with clinical severity variables and with established expression-derived taxonomies, but the agreement is not strong. TCGA m1-m4 and ClearCode34 overlap the RNA discovery view, so these are taxonomy correspondence analyses, not independent validation. The clinical associations are statistical and do not establish clinical utility or prognosis.
